newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - MAY 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - MAY 6.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:
KATHIMERINI

--Speedier promotion of structural reforms in privatisation and the job market are the first things being recommended by the members of the International Monetary Fund delegation, in Athens since yesterday to research their report on the course of the Greek economy.
--A new surge ahead at the Athens Stock Exchange at yesterday's session with the general price index breaking the 1,500 barrier to close up 2.25 percent and trade reaching 22.1 billion drachmas.

--Athens Paper Mills "Softex" is facing closure at the same time as efforts for its privatisation get under way. New financing to continue operating will not be forthcoming from creditor banks without guarantees from the state.
IMERISIA

--The government has committed itself to bringing inflation down to 5.0 percent by July, in talks with the visiting IMF delegation. This development would lay the groundwork for a new round of interest rate cuts ahead of the summer.
--OTE, Greece's telecoms organisation, is expected to submit its prospectus on the sewcond share offer immediately after OTE's general assembly on May 29.
--European bankers will meet this week in Athens.
KERDOS
--Buying interest on yesterday's session at the bourse was centred on banks and OTE, in anticipation of competitive prices for new shares to be exchanged for old.
--Concerns over the course of inflows have abated since April, with figures allowing contained optimism about the final result. First quarter 1997 saw inflows reach 650 billion drachmas.
--The Macedonia-Thrace Bank will rechedule debts by private firms on favourable terms in an effort to restructure its portfolio.
NAFTEMBORIKI

--The IMF delegation has seen positive economic developments with full agreement between the IMF and the government on the course of inflation and growth but there is still concern over the goal of reducing the budget deficit to 4.2 percent of GDP.
--The euro is causing major headaches for European multinationals, with only 12 percent prepared to adopt the euro on January 1, 1999.
EXPRESS

--The construction of the Athens Metro is up in the air as the dispute between the construction company and the government comes to a head. Olympic Metro yesterday ordered work on one station to stop.
--OTE's administration will present its plans the second share offer to the Athens Stock Exchange authorities today.
--Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
